details:
THE SILENT WITNESSES – ABANDONED BUT NOT FORGOTTEN

Project Overview

The Silent Witnesses is a digital storytelling project developed by Team CASIO to explore the equipment and human-made objects left behind during space exploration missions on the Moon and Mars.

Space missions require several types of equipment, including landing stages, scientific instruments, parachutes, protective shells and other mission hardware. Some of these objects remain on planetary surfaces even after their primary missions are completed.

How Our Project Works

Our project presents real examples of discarded space equipment through an informative digital presentation and interactive website. It focuses on historical Apollo lunar mission equipment and the parachute and backshell separated during NASA's Perseverance rover landing on Mars. It explains why these objects were used, why they remained behind and what scientific or historical value they hold.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project helps people understand the lesser-known side of space exploration. It increases awareness of space history, engineering achievements and the importance of preserving significant locations on the Moon and Mars for future exploration. It also encourages students to explore planetary science and aerospace engineering.

Tools and Technologies

The project uses digital research, HTML, CSS, web technologies and presentation software to organize information and communicate the story. NASA-related public resources and scientific datasets are used as references.

Creativity and Innovation

Instead of focusing only on successful space missions, our project tells the story of the equipment that remains after those missions. By presenting these objects as silent witnesses to human exploration, we connect engineering, science and history through storytelling.
